11	def log_returns(prices: Prices) -> Returns:
12	    """Each ticker's return from one date to the next; ValueError with fewer than two dates."""
13	    if len(prices.dates) < 2:
14	        raise ValueError(f"need at least two dates for returns, got {len(prices.dates)}")
15	    values = {
16	        ticker: tuple(now / before - 1.0 for before, now in pairwise(prices.closes[ticker]))
17	        for ticker in prices.tickers
18	    }
19	    return Returns(
20	        base_date=prices.dates[0],
21	        dates=prices.dates[1:],
22	        tickers=prices.tickers,
23	        values=values,
24	    )

"""Unit tests for the returns step: daily log returns."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from mdata import Prices
from risk.returns import log_returns
from risk.types import Returns

pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit

LN2 = 0.6931471805599453


def test_returns_drop_the_first_date_as_base():
    prices = Prices(
        dates=("2024-01-02", "2024-01-03", "2024-01-04"),
        tickers=("A", "B"),
        closes={"A": (100.0, 200.0, 100.0), "B": (50.0, 50.0, 25.0)},
    )
    returns = log_returns(prices)
    assert isinstance(returns, Returns)
    assert returns.base_date == "2024-01-02"
    assert returns.dates == ("2024-01-03", "2024-01-04")
    assert returns.tickers == ("A", "B")
    assert returns.values["A"] == pytest.approx((LN2, -LN2), abs=1e-15)
    assert returns.values["B"] == pytest.approx((0.0, -LN2), abs=1e-15)


def test_log_returns_differ_from_simple_returns():
    prices = Prices(dates=("d1", "d2"), tickers=("A",), closes={"A": (100.0, 110.0)})
    (r,) = log_returns(prices).values["A"]
    assert r == pytest.approx(0.09531017980432493, abs=1e-15)
    assert r != pytest.approx(0.1, abs=1e-6)


def test_returns_need_two_dates():
    prices = Prices(dates=("2024-01-02",), tickers=("A",), closes={"A": (100.0,)})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="two dates"):
        log_returns(prices)

from mdata import Prices
from risk.returns import log_returns
from risk.types import Returns

pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit

LN2 = 0.6931471805599453


def test_returns_drop_the_first_date_as_base():
    prices = Prices(
        dates=("2024-01-02", "2024-01-03", "2024-01-04"),
        tickers=("A", "B"),
        closes={"A": (100.0, 200.0, 100.0), "B": (50.0, 50.0, 25.0)},
    )
    returns = log_returns(prices)
    assert isinstance(returns, Returns)
    assert returns.base_date == "2024-01-02"
    assert returns.dates == ("2024-01-03", "2024-01-04")
    assert returns.tickers == ("A", "B")
    assert returns.values["A"] == pytest.approx((LN2, -LN2), abs=1e-15)
    assert returns.values["B"] == pytest.approx((0.0, -LN2), abs=1e-15)


def test_log_returns_differ_from_simple_returns():
    prices = Prices(dates=("d1", "d2"), tickers=("A",), closes={"A": (100.0, 110.0)})
    (r,) = log_returns(prices).values["A"]
    assert r == pytest.approx(0.09531017980432493, abs=1e-15)
    assert r != pytest.approx(0.1, abs=1e-6)


def test_returns_need_two_dates():
    prices = Prices(dates=("2024-01-02",), tickers=("A",), closes={"A": (100.0,)})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="two dates"):
        log_returns(prices)
